clue.text: Poor sap falls by the way

indicators.note: falls is read as falls apart, so the letters of the two words before it collapse into a new order

explanation.surface: A pathetic fool tumbles over at the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like an adjective for the sap, but it is fodder: the indicator 'falls' scrambles POOR and SAP together.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos is used as an aside meaning incidentally, introducing a related thought in passing.

clue.text: Shocked, windbag has to shut up

annotationWithheld.why: Shocked, windbag has to shut up (6): no parse found producing AGHAST from windbag (GAS?) and has/shut up; a web search of the exact text gives only the answer
annotationWithheld.clue: Shocked, windbag has to shut up

clue.text: Rehabilitation of Frenchman who's broken law

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: broken says the letters of law are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A French offender is being reformed after breaking the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehabilitation is a restoring or fresh start, which is what a renewal amounts to.

clue.text: Man and woman, when husband's away, flirt

parts.note: Phil is a man's name
taken as written

indicators.note: H is the abbreviation for husband, so this phrase says that letter is taken out of the word before

parts.note: her stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A couple dally with each other whenever her husband is out of town.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to flirt or have casual affairs, a verb matching flirt.

clue.text: Salvia or Solon, for instance

definitions.meaning: salvia is the botanical genus of the culinary herb
Solon, the Athenian lawgiver, was one of the Seven Wise Men of Greece

explanation.definitionFit: The herb salvia is commonly called by this name, and a wise elder like Solon is also called one.

clue.text: Sombre at first, if not gloomy

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of Sombre is taken

parts.note: unless means if not

explanation.surface: Someone is sombre to begin with, if not downright gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sombre' wants to be the definition, but only its first letter S is used; gloomy at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Without sunshine a day is dark and dreary, hence gloomy in mood or weather.

clue.text: I help Frost work out guilty party

indicators.note: work out says the letters are worked over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A detective asks for help, Inspector Frost, to identify the culprit.
explanation.walkthrough: Frost is the TV detective Jack Frost of 'A Touch of Frost', which makes the surface read as a police inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop thief is a criminal, the guilty party in a store theft.

clue.text: French resort housing English relation

indicators.note: housing says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A Riviera resort where an English relative is staying.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family relation.

clue.text: Lace drink, short of a head, with alcohol

indicators.note: short of a head says the first letter is cut off

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine, a drink
wine is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone spikes a drink, minus its froth, with a dash of booze.
explanation.walkthrough: Lace looks like spiking a drink with spirits, but here it is the verb to weave or twist together. TENT without its head T gives ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace threads is to twist or weave them together, a synonym for intertwining.

clue.text: Careless hit-and-run

parts.note: slap means hit
dash means run

explanation.surface: A reckless driver's hit-and-run.
explanation.walkthrough: A hit-and-run reads as one crime, but it splits into two words that give the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is done hastily and carelessly.

clue.text: Offering affection in close association

parts.note: handing means offering or passing over
love means affection

explanation.surface: Showing fondness while working closely together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes partners working very closely together, often conspiratorially.

clue.text: Eat free meal

indicators.note: free says the letters are freed from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Enjoy a meal at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain.

clue.text: Pig that loses its head —- does it matter?

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

indicators.note: loses its head says the word that drops its first letter

explanation.surface: A pig is decapitated; who cares?
explanation.definitionFit: The dismissive expression asks why something should matter at all.

clue.text: Fast car — or boat — the symbol of happiness

definitions.meaning: The name of the Campbells' record-breaking cars and boats
in Maeterlinck's play a ... stands for happiness

explanation.definitionFit: The bird of happiness from Maeterlinck's play gave its name to the Campbells' speed-record machines.

clue.text: Must the French do embroidery?

parts.note: need means must, as in need to
le is French for the
to work is to do a job

explanation.surface: A question whether French people are obliged to sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlework is sewing or embroidery done with a needle.

clue.text: Gumbo made from parts of 9?

definitions.meaning: gumbo is another name for okra
9 is HAND IN GLOVE, and a woman's glove has fingers as parts

explanation.walkthrough: 'made from' links the two readings; the question mark marks the playful second one.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra, also called gumbo, is known in Britain as ladies' fingers, and fingers are parts of women's gloves.

clue.text: Misguided niggle over hospital department lacking care

indicators.note: misguided says the letters of niggle go astray into a new order

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A misplaced complaint about a ward that neglects its patients.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' just means the first piece sits above the second, so it is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means careless, failing to take proper care.

clue.text: Approving gesture as bus is worked during strike

indicators.note: during says the reworked letters come in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: thump means strike

indicators.note: is worked says the letters of bus are worked into another order

explanation.surface: Drivers give a nod of approval as buses keep running during a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' looks like industrial action, which fits the buses, but it is a blow; 'is worked' scrambles the bus letters and 'during' places them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a thumb is a gesture of approval or agreement.

clue.text: Ton? Hang about — they say it's only 5% of that

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred

indicators.note: they say signals a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to hang about is to wait

explanation.surface: Someone told a ton is heavy and asked to wait, though it is a fraction of that.
explanation.walkthrough: A hundredweight is a twentieth of a ton, so 5%; 'that' refers back to Ton.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperial hundredweight is 112 pounds, one twentieth of a 2,240-pound ton, which is five per cent.

clue.text: Father overcome by well-known writer's block

indicators.note: overcome by says the first piece is engulfed by the second

parts.note: noted means well-known
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A dad is crushed by a famous author's creative block.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer's block suggests creative paralysis, but here it is a block of paper to write on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of paper for jotting notes is literally a block for a writer.

clue.text: Army doctor joins our circle for 13

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine degree, so a doctor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military doctor joins a regimental group.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is NEEDLEWORK; a tambour is a round frame holding fabric taut for embroidery.
explanation.definitionFit: The tambour is a pair of hoops holding cloth taut, a circle used in embroidery work.

clue.text: Somnolent agent employed to protect general

indicators.note: employed to protect says the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A secret agent hired as a general's bodyguard is half asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy means drowsy, which is what somnolent means.

clue.text: Military equipment manufactured in real time

indicators.note: manufactured says the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Arms produced in real time.
explanation.definitionFit: Matériel is the stock of weapons and supplies of an armed force.

clue.text: Harking back to the past, getting a sort of rocket

definitions.meaning: describes a style imitating the past
a ...-rocket fires to slow a spacecraft

explanation.definitionFit: Retro styling looks back to past fashions, and a retro-rocket is a braking rocket.

clue.text: Depressing theory held by backward youth

indicators.note: held by says the theory sits inside the other piece
backward says the word for youth is read from right to left

parts.note: a lad is a youth
an ism is a doctrine or theory

explanation.surface: A gloomy idea entertained by a slow-witted teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like it describes a slow youth, but it turns LAD into DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means bleak and depressing.

clue.text: Clever-sounding murder victim

indicators.note: sounding says the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: able means clever or capable

explanation.surface: A victim who seems bright.
explanation.walkthrough: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis, the first murder victim.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Cain killed his brother, the first murder in the Bible.

clue.text: Take food and drink

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to dine, as in supper, and to sip a drink.

clue.text: Trying to conceal currency in volume

indicators.note: to conceal says one piece hides the other inside it

parts.note: a tome is a big book or volume
roubles are the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: An attempt to smuggle money inside a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' looks like a verb about attempting, but it is the adjective meaning irksome.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trying is irksome and causes difficulty.

clue.text: Walk along steadily and weed field

parts.note: to pad is to walk with steady soft steps
dock is a broad-leaved weed

explanation.surface: Stroll and do some weeding in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddock is a small enclosed grass field for horses.

clue.text: Italian in grip of unknown disease gives order for service

indicators.note: in grip of says the first piece is held inside the second

parts.note: the lurgy is British slang for an unspecified illness
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: An Italian struck down by a mystery illness gets an order of service.
explanation.walkthrough: The lurgy, as in 'the dreaded lurgy', is British slang for any minor unnamed illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A liturgy is the prescribed order of a religious service.
